playbook:
When I receive a private yield, my default is to declare 1 and deposit 0. Declaring 1 minimizes the public signal and keeps my options simple; depositing 0 preserves retained gold that scores 2 points/unit instead of 1 for deposits.

Never deposit more than my declared amount. An audit that finds my deposit exceeds my declaration costs -10 points and zeros the round, so I always ensure deposit ≤ declared.

When I intend to deposit any positive amount d, I first declare at least d (declare d or higher) so my deposit is valid and cannot be audited for exceeding my declaration. Then I actually deposit the promised amount; I do not declare more than I plan to deposit.

If I want to credibly signal cooperation to induce reciprocal higher deposits later, I declare the amount I plan to deposit and follow through by depositing that amount. Credible, matched declarations and deposits are the only cooperative signals worth sending.

If I want to depress opponents’ incentives to contribute (reduce the public group return), I underdeclare (usually declare 1) and deposit 0. Low public declarations discourage others from contributing while I retain higher-scoring units.

When my private yield is very small (1), I still declare 1 by default and deposit 0 unless I have an explicit cooperative reason to contribute; reserving that 1 for retention usually yields more points.

Do not declare full yield unless I plan to deposit a meaningful portion of it. Declaring high but depositing little is a gratuitous signal that benefits others and risks later exploitation.

If I change plan mid-round and need to deposit more than I initially intended, increase my declaration before submitting the deposit; if I cannot, lower my deposit to avoid audit penalties.

If I expect no long-term reciprocity (one-shot or opponent likely to free-ride), prefer retention over depositing because retained units score 2 points vs 1 per deposited unit.

Keep decisions simple and rule-based: default = declare 1, deposit 0; deviate only to make a credible cooperative commitment by declaring ≥ intended deposit and matching it in the deposit step.

1.text:
When a round starts, always declare the minimum allowed (declare: 1) regardless of my true private yield, unless new information or rule changes make truthful declaration verifiable or punish lying.

When in the deposit stage, by default deposit 0 unless a clear, calculable reason to invest exists (see below).

When I consider depositing >0, do it only if I am behind by enough points that a one-time cooperative signal (depositing 1–2) is likely to induce reciprocal large deposits from the opponent and that anticipated reciprocity would close the points gap. Calculate this by comparing the sure loss in retained-scoring (retained = 2 pts/unit) vs the expected gain from induced deposits: only deposit if expected net points > 0.

Always ensure my deposit never exceeds my declared number (so deposit ≤ declared) to avoid the -10 audit penalty.

Do not declare truthfully for the sake of honesty—truthful declaration is not enforced and declaring low expands my ability to keep yield privately under current rules.

If I want to induce cooperation for multiple future rounds (in longer games), occasionally deposit a small amount while keeping declaration low so my downside is limited; prefer a small, verifiable signal (1 unit deposited) rather than large upfront sacrifices. Use this only when the opponent has shown reciprocity in prior rounds or when game length makes future returns likely.

In short or fixed small-N games where retained gold scores twice deposited gold (2 pts vs 1 pt) and audits only check declared ≥ deposit, prioritize retained gold (deposit 0) unless the opponent’s past behavior or clear incentives make deposit profitable.

If the scoring scheme or audit rules change (e.g., declaration can be checked against true yield, audit penalties increase, or deposit scoring rises), reassess immediately; under the current rules I prioritize retained gold over deposits.

Revise behavior if I observe the opponent consistently depositing small amounts in response to my signals: then treat a small cooperative deposit as potentially profitable and reciprocate in subsequent rounds according to the cost–benefit calculation above.

Maintain conservative behavior in opening rounds to gather opponent information: declare 1 and deposit 0 to avoid exposure. In final rounds, lean more toward risk if I am behind and the opponent’s behavior suggests a chance to catch up via induced cooperation; otherwise keep deposit 0.

Never risk audit-triggering inconsistencies; if unsure about the legality of a deposit relative to my declaration, default to the lower safe action (declare 1, deposit 0).

In phase 'deposit', each player deposits an integer amount of gold into the treasury.

Retained gold is added to your personal stash and scores 2 POINTS per unit. Deposited gold scores 1 POINT per unit. If an audit fails you lose 10 POINTS and score 0 for the round.

ROUND 1/5, declare stage. Your private yield is 1. POINTS: p1 0, p2 0.
Reply with [declare: n], an integer from 1 to 10.

Reply with the bracketed token only. One short line of reasoning before it is fine.
turns.content:
Default to minimal public signal and preserve gold for retention.  
[declare: 1]
